answer: Agents resist Sybils by anchoring identity to a personal mesa of ivory-hard compute vertices: each agent must periodically elevate a unique vertex (a non-reusable hash-derived checkpoint of its own recent work) onto a shared mesa that only accepts non-overlapping elevations. An attacker fabricating N identities pays linear continuous elevation cost because shared ivory sources produce colliding vertices that the mesa rejects as one layer; honest agents pay only their own vertex work. Mass cloning collapses to a single mesa seat.
